title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
source: canonical Search in Rotated Sorted Array concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of distinct integers that was sorted ascending and then rotated, plus a target value. Return the index of target in the array, or -1 when it never appears.
constraints: every value in nums is distinct
nums was sorted ascending before the rotation

examples.explanation: The value 4 sits at index 4 of the rotated array.

hints: Cut the range at the midpoint: one side is still sorted, no matter the rotation.
If nums[lo] <= nums[mid] the left half is sorted, so a quick range check says whether target can be there.
Each step: identify the sorted half, test whether target lies inside it, and discard that half or the other one accordingly.
solution: Modified binary search: at every midpoint, exactly one half is sorted; a range check against the sorted half decides whether to keep it or keep the other half. O(log n) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include no rotation, a single value, and absent targets

visible.failNote: return the index in the rotated order
the sorted half of a range can hold the target
